statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete: all 58 checks judged across five representative paths.

page.framework: Laravel/server-rendered HTML with Bootstrap-style CSS and a small ES module
page.notes: Public multilingual downloader/PWA. Coverage included the core Instagram tool, sibling Reels and TikTok templates, contact form, and Arabic localization. Near-identical photo/story/highlight routes and every locale were not repeated because they share templates.

paths.description: English Instagram video downloader landing page and primary one-step URL form; represents the main downloader template.
Instagram Reels downloader; sampled as a sibling downloader archetype and not duplicated across every near-identical Instagram route.
TikTok downloader; represents the second platform-specific downloader template.
Contact form; represents the secondary form, support, and recovery surface.
Arabic locale; represents the 21 linked non-English localized variants and tests language/direction metadata.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures every primary surface on first load
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots on the home, Reels, TikTok, contact, and Arabic paths show a modal consent wall before the downloader or form can be used. On mobile it fills most of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential advertising until a choice, keep equal accept/reject controls, and replace the blocking first-load wall with a compact, content-preserving consent surface where legally permissible.

findings.summary: Consent UI is a custom div dialog rather than a native dialog primitive
findings.evidence: DOM evidence identifies .fc-consent-root containing a div role=dialog and a separate overlay; no <dialog>, popover, or details primitives exist on the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> for the modal consent flow, with platform focus containment, Escape handling, and explicit close/reject semantics.

findings.summary: Theme is hard-coded dark instead of following the user color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Light and dark emulation screenshots retain the same dark #212529 page surface; DOM computed styles report color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and drive surface/text tokens from prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving sufficient contrast in both themes.

findings.summary: A decorative animation continues under reduced-motion
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports a running color-change animation with 1000ms duration even though prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable the decorative color-change animation in the reduce query, not only Bootstrap transitions.

findings.summary: Primary brand, tab, and heading colours fail WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports contrast ratios of 2.22:1 to 2.69:1 for the brand, active tabs, H1, and H2 text against dark surfaces, below required 3:1 or 4.5:1 thresholds.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the dark blue/purple text token with a lighter accessible token and verify normal and large text in all theme states.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inconsistent, and heading order skips levels
findings.evidence: The focus probe shows the navbar toggle, URL input, search button, and FAQ buttons with outline none while focused; many navigation targets are 20-40px tall. Lighthouse also reports an invalid H2-to-H4 heading order.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible style, keep 44px target sizing/spacing, and correct the heading hierarchy without using heading ranks for styling.

findings.summary: Route and state changes lack authored transition/attention cues
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no authored transition components, anchor positioning, or scroll timelines; navigation is conventional full-document links and the sampled FAQ/menu state uses Bootstrap-style abrupt state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and meaningful state changes with same/cross-document View Transitions and preserve reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Reusable downloader components rely only on viewport layout
findings.evidence: CSSOM probing found zero CSSContainerRule entries even though the downloader/form/navigation components recur across templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable tool panels a containment context and use @container for local adaptations, retaining viewport rules as fallback.

findings.summary: Downloader failure and recovery states are not exposed accessibly
findings.evidence: The primary URL field has no label or aria-invalid state, and the invalid submission navigation closed the inspected target without an in-place role=alert or recoverable error captured.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, keep the user on the form, announce a specific error in a live region, preserve the entered URL, and provide retry guidance.

findings.summary: Largest content paint and layout stability miss the good range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.1s and CLS 0.225; the mobile layout primitive independently observed CLS 0.205. TBT remained low at 100ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the real LCP content, reserve space for consent/ad/image regions, and prevent late UI insertion from shifting the page.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising and analytics dominate bytes and unused code
findings.evidence: HAR records 930,902 transferred bytes, 821,879 third-party bytes and 805,862 script bytes. Lighthouse estimates 370 KiB unused JS and 45 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Load advertising/analytics only after consent and when an ad slot is near use, remove duplicate UA/GA4 payloads, subset font CSS, and split page-specific CSS/JS.

findings.summary: Images lack dimensions and third-party code uses deprecated APIs
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all three images without width/height and two legacy JPEGs; Lighthouse reports three deprecated API warnings from the Cloudflare challenge script.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio and responsive modern image sources; update or reconfigure the third-party challenge integration to remove deprecated API use.

findings.summary: Rich entity and social-preview metadata are absent
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter card tags on the public downloader page, despite a canonical URL and rich tool/organization content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite/WebApplication JSON-LD plus Open Graph and Twitter preview tags that match visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no CSP or HSTS, and no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence reports six non-Secure analytics/consent cookies and SameSite=None usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, HSTS, strict referrer and permissions policies; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: Tracking starts with a broad third-party footprint before a consent choice
findings.evidence: Trackers evidence finds 10 third-party origins and four known tracker domains; HAR assigns 20 requests and 821,879 bytes to third parties while the consent wall is still present.
findings.suggestedFix: Block analytics and advertising requests before affirmative consent, minimise vendors and event collection, and batch only necessary measurements.

findings.summary: Installed PWA has no offline fallback for core pages
findings.evidence: A manifest and active service worker exist, but serviceworker.js caches only six icon files and falls through to fetch() for every page without an offline response.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache an offline fallback page and core shell/content; handle navigation fetch failures explicitly while keeping network-first freshness where needed.

findings.summary: Arabic pages omit RTL direction metadata
findings.evidence: The Arabic path correctly sets lang=ar and exposes hreflang links, but documentElement.dir is empty while the visible content is Arabic.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl on Arabic documents and migrate layout spacing/alignment to logical properties; regression-test mixed-direction URLs and numbers.

findings.summary: Forms depend on placeholders and omit durable labels/autocomplete assistance
findings.evidence: The contact DOM shows required email and message controls with placeholders but no associated labels or aria-labels; email autocomplete is empty. The downloader URL input also has no label and autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels and appropriate autocomplete tokens (email, url where useful), then provide post-interaction, accessible required-field feedback.

findings.summary: The fixed theme has no high-contrast adaptation and already loses essential contrast
findings.evidence: CSS evidence contains reduced-motion rules but no prefers-contrast or forced-colors adaptation, while Lighthouse directly identifies essential tabs, headings, and brand text at only 2.22:1 to 2.69:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for essential controls and text, use system colors where appropriate, and verify custom scrollbars and focus indicators remain visible.

taskList.title: Stop advertising and analytics before affirmative consent; reduce the vendor/script footprint
Fix LCP and CLS by reserving late content and prioritising the actual main content
Repair contrast, focus-visible, target sizing, heading structure, and durable form labels
Deploy CSP/HSTS/policy headers and correct cookie security attributes
Make Arabic truly RTL with dir and logical layout properties
Add recoverable, announced downloader and form error states
Respect light/dark, reduced-motion, and high-contrast user preferences
Add a real offline fallback to the installed PWA
Modernise images and remove deprecated/unused assets
Add structured data and social preview metadata
Progressively enhance route/state navigation and component responsiveness
Use a native semantic dialog and reduce consent-wall obstruction
